- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing downside.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast overshoot at +15% above recent 7-day high.
- After a sharp price rise, model frequently fails to correct downward; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 2–5% of the spike from next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overfits noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before major moves.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean; apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.3 → -1.0 → +0.6), model misreads momentum; reduce forecast slope by 30–50% in such regimes.
